clue.text: One expecting advice here about a forthcoming issue?

definitions.text: One expecting advice here about a forthcoming issue?

parts.words: One expecting advice here about a forthcoming issue?
parts.note: 'One expecting' is a pregnant woman and the 'forthcoming issue' is her baby, not a magazine edition, so this is a place offering pre-birth care

explanation.surface: Someone awaiting guidance on an upcoming edition or problem asks where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a matter for discussion or a publication; here it means offspring, and 'expecting' means pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant mother attends a clinic before the birth for checks and guidance.

clue.text: See a dish, eastern, is cooked when necessary

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of the preceding words are prepared afresh and mixed

explanation.surface: Diners are invited to view an eastern dish, prepared whenever required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the fifteen letters of SEE A DISH EASTERN; 'is' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for doing something only at the moment a requirement turns up.

clue.text: TA member in row about blunder

indicators.note: about tells us one word goes round the other, the row enclosing the mistake

parts.note: a row of seats is a tier
to blunder is to err

explanation.surface: A Territorial Army soldier in a row of seats makes a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; a member is nicknamed a 'Terrier', which also suggests the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Territorial Army reserve force were familiarly called by this dog-breed nickname.

clue.text: Unfamiliar breed of dairy cattle in this US state

parts.note: something unfamiliar is new to you
Jersey cows are a dairy breed from the Channel Island

explanation.surface: An odd kind of milk cow is found in this American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A state on the American east coast, between New York and Pennsylvania.

clue.text: Strengthened part of next one down

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to point at the following entry in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to refer to the clue below, but the letters sit inside 'nexT ONE Down'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned muscles are firmed up and made stronger by exercise.

clue.text: Crayfish in sea -no glut, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately hints that things have gone wrong, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Shellfish are scarce in the sea, with no glut, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges SEANOGLUT, the nine letters of 'sea no glut'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny lobster, known in French by this name, is a kind of crayfish.

clue.text: Free hire travel

parts.note: to let a property is to hire it out
to travel is to go

explanation.surface: Cheap rental means no-cost transport.
explanation.definitionFit: To release someone is to stop holding them, an idiomatic sense of setting free.

clue.text: Climbing up once more, artist falls

indicators.note: climbing up in a down entry means the word for once more is written from bottom to top

parts.note: once more means again
RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist scaling a height again takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing up' turns AGAIN into NIAGA; RA stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Secret letter she translated in northern town

indicators.note: translated suggests the words are turned into another form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coded message she decoded in a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges the fifteen letters of SECRET LETTER SHE. The answer is a town in County Durham, north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in County Durham in the north-east of England.

clue.text: The endless falling-out at home causes one to interject

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word The is dropped

parts.note: a falling-out is a row, a quarrel
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A domestic quarrel prompts someone to butt in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw in a remark is to add it casually to a conversation, an idiom for interjecting.

clue.text: Fruitcake, fanatic on box

parts.note: a fanatic or enthusiast is a nut
a box is a case

explanation.surface: A fruitcake, beloved of an enthusiast, sits on a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' looks like a cake; it is slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal slang for a crazy or eccentric person.

clue.text: The best stretch of thoroughfare, lit extensively

indicators.note: stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The finest part of a well-illuminated main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in 'thoroughfarE, LIT Extensively'.
explanation.definitionFit: The top group of any society or field are its choicest members.

clue.text: Antiperspirant, too darned smelly!

indicators.note: smelly hints at something off, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs and complains that their antiperspirant is far too pungent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smelly' rearranges TOODARNED, the letters of 'too darned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiperspirants are commonly sold combined with an odour-masking product of this kind.

clue.text: An ancient people using runes, cast out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old civilisation practising divination by casting runes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RUNESCAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-Roman civilisation of central Italy.

clue.text: One practising self-denial in a British town? Almost right

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the town name is left off

parts.note: Staines is a town in Surrey, west of London

explanation.surface: Someone living austerely in an English town, which is nearly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a Surrey town near Heathrow; 'Almost' trims it to STAINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller or anyone refraining from indulgences avoids pleasures by choice.

clue.text: Opening of Coward musical-seat's required

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of Coward is taken

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: A Noel Coward musical's premiere requires a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture for one person to sit on.

clue.text: Flying to a place inhabited by king and queen

indicators.note: inhabited by means the jumbled letters have the king's letter living inside them
flying suggests the words are in motion, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Flying off to a place where a king and queen live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' rearranges TOAPLACE and 'inhabited by' puts R inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The last ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt was a famous queen.

clue.text: Slightly eccentric little girl

definitions.meaning: a mildly crazy person is a bit daft
a pet form of the girl's name Dorothy

explanation.surface: A rather odd young lass.
explanation.definitionFit: It means mildly crazy, and is also the familiar form of Dorothy, a girl's name.

clue.text: Porwiggle in Po Delta, developing

indicators.note: developing implies growth and change, so the letters of Po Delta are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young frog-to-be grows up in the delta of an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges PODELTA. Porwiggle is an old dialect word for a young frog.
explanation.definitionFit: Porwiggle is an old name for the larva of a frog or toad.

clue.text: Boy with note concerning docker

parts.note: Steve is a boy's name
do is a note of the sol-fa scale
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A lad writes a memo about a dock worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at the docks.

clue.text: Use to perform surgery

definitions.meaning: to use a machine is to run it
surgeons cut open patients in theatre

explanation.surface: Use the knife to do surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: It means to work a machine and also for a surgeon to cut into a patient.

clue.text: No longer needed to go on about duke, exposed in retreat

indicators.note: about means the rant goes around the other letters

parts.note: to go on at length is to rant

indicators.note: in retreat means the duke and the exposed word together go backwards

parts.note: exposed means naked, nude

explanation.surface: Someone rants about a duke who stripped off while on a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reverses the duke and the naked word together, giving EDUND, and 'about' wraps the ranting word round it. 'retreat' looks like a hideaway but signals going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Surplus to requirements, as a worker laid off when a job vanishes.

clue.text: Former PM giving direction

definitions.meaning: one of the four compass points

explanation.surface: An ex-premier giving instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North led the British government during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: A Prime Minister of the 18th century and one of the compass points.

clue.text: Prison sentence beginning to slip by

parts.note: serving time is serving a prison sentence

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of slip is taken

explanation.surface: A jail term starts to slide by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is the multiplication sense: three by four is three times four.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic 'multiplied by' and this word are interchangeable.

clue.text: Gather in place to dine

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Assemble at a location for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' looks like a verb for assembling; it is a fold sewn into fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressmaking, both are folds stitched into cloth.

clue.text: Son with new apron containing bit of room for pouch

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged apron holds a letter inside
new means the letters of apron are made over into a fresh order
bit of means just the first letter of room

explanation.surface: A boy in a new apron holds a small part of the room as a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges APRON to PORAN and 'containing' puts R inside: PORRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish Highland dress pouch worn in front of the kilt.

clue.text: Written by me, article about an odourless gas

indicators.note: about means the article goes around the next word

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: I have written a piece about a gas with no smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the indefinite article inside the definite one, giving THANE; 'Written by me' places the pronoun before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural gas is mostly this colourless, scentless hydrocarbon.

clue.text: This Schubert song helps mend hearts, broken

indicators.note: broken suggests the words are smashed and the pieces put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A Schubert lied soothes broken hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges HELPSMENDHEARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Schäfers Klagelied is one of Schubert's early songs, known under this English title.
